title: High Pressure Switch Open

fixSteps.title: Service diagnostics
fixSteps.instruction: Use Rheem service tool to read fault history.

whenToCallPro: Sealed system or inverter board work needs a licensed Rheem dealer.

title: Communication Loss

title: Reversing Valve Failure
shortDescription: Reversing valve did not shift on command.
fullDescription: AC11 indicates the EcoNet board commanded a mode change but coil temperatures did not respond — reversing valve stuck.

fixSteps.title: Tap Valve
fixSteps.instruction: Gently strike valve body during call.

faq.a: Yes — reversing valves are top-3 heat-pump failures.

title: Defrost Sensor Fault
fullDescription: AC12 means the defrost thermistor reading is invalid — heat pump cannot enter defrost properly.
whenToCallPro: If sensor and wiring check out, defrost board needs service.

faq.a: Defrost is heat-pump specific; AC-only models don't fault here.

title: EXV Stall
shortDescription: Electronic expansion valve out of step.
fullDescription: AC13 reports an EXV step-count error — the valve isn't tracking commanded position.

faq.a: Electronic Expansion Valve — replaces traditional TXV in modern heat pumps.

title: Compressor Discharge Sensor Fault
fullDescription: AC14 indicates the compressor discharge temperature sensor reading is out of range.
whenToCallPro: Suspect outdoor board if sensor checks out.

title: Compressor Discharge Over-Temp
fullDescription: AC15 fires when discharge temperature is too high — compressor lockout follows to prevent oil breakdown.

faq.a: Yes — until root cause is fixed.

title: Outdoor Fan Speed Mismatch
shortDescription: Condenser fan RPM out of range.
fullDescription: AC16 indicates the outdoor ECM fan is not running at the commanded speed.

fixSteps.title: Manual Check
fixSteps.instruction: Power off; spin fan by hand.

faq.a: ECM-style fans don't use external run caps.

title: Inverter Over-Temp
fullDescription: AC17 is set when the variable-speed compressor inverter heat sink reaches thermal limits.

faq.q: Why summer issue on heat pump?
faq.a: Inverter is hot during cooling AND heating mode.

title: Inverter Bus Voltage Fault
shortDescription: DC bus voltage out of range.
fullDescription: AC18 indicates the inverter DC bus is outside operating spec — usually a power-electronics failure.

faq.a: Yes — recommended for inverter heat pumps.

safetyWarning: Inverter caps hold lethal voltage. Verify with meter before touching.

title: Indoor Airflow Insufficient
fullDescription: AC19 reports the indoor blower cannot achieve required CFM at any tap.

fixSteps.title: Open Registers
fixSteps.instruction: Walk house and open all supply vents.

faq.q: How many registers can I close?
faq.a: No more than 20% of total CFM.

title: EcoNet Communications Lost
fullDescription: AC20 fires when the EcoNet bus link to the thermostat drops.

faq.a: Some EcoNet outdoor units don't support legacy 24V mode.

title: AC21 — Inverter Drive Communication Loss
shortDescription: EcoNet outdoor unit lost CAN-bus to inverter drive.
fullDescription: Rheem EcoNet/Prestige inverter heat pumps use CAN-bus between control board and inverter drive. AC21 means CAN packets stopped for >5 sec.

faq.a: Yes - CAN-bus needs twisted shielded pair.

title: AC22 — Compressor Drive Overcurrent
shortDescription: Inverter drive measured compressor amps above limit.
fullDescription: AC22 fires when Rheem inverter drive sees compressor current exceed nameplate. Causes: liquid flood-back, mechanical bind, or low voltage.

faq.a: Warming compressor to boil off liquid before start.

title: AC23 — Reversing Valve Sense Fail
shortDescription: Mode change commanded but coil temps did not flip.
fullDescription: AC23 means after a heat/cool mode change, Rheem EcoNet did not see the expected temperature swap between liquid and suction sensors within 90 sec.

faq.a: Valve body stuck rare on new units, more common after 10+ years.

title: AC24 — DC Bus Voltage Low
shortDescription: Inverter drive DC bus below operating threshold.
fullDescription: AC24 indicates inverter drive bus capacitors not maintaining voltage. Causes: aged capacitors, low line voltage, or failed rectifier diodes.
safetyWarning: DC bus retains charge after power-off.

title: AC25 — Discharge Temperature High
fullDescription: AC25 protects the compressor: discharge above 250F = low charge, dirty filter, or TXV stuck.

faq.a: Compressor windings degrade above 250F discharge - address quickly.

title: AC26 — Outdoor Fan Locked Rotor
shortDescription: ECM outdoor fan reported locked rotor.
fullDescription: AC26 fires when Rheem ECM outdoor fan attempts start but cannot rotate.

title: AC27 — Outdoor Coil Sensor Drift
fullDescription: AC27 is a soft fault: outdoor coil thermistor reads suspicious value vs. ambient. Often a loose strap.

title: AC28 — Demand Defrost Algorithm Fault
shortDescription: Defrost ran max time 3x without clearing coil.
fullDescription: AC28 indicates Rheem demand-defrost algorithm cannot complete defrost. 3 consecutive failures = lockout.

title: AC29 — Liquid Line Sensor Open
fullDescription: AC29 means the liquid line sensor used for charge calculation is invalid. Charge monitoring disabled.

fixSteps.title: Inspect
fixSteps.instruction: On liquid line at outdoor unit.

title: AC30 — EcoNet Comm Loss to Indoor
shortDescription: Outdoor lost EcoNet communication with indoor.
fullDescription: AC30 fires when Rheem EcoNet 4-wire bus (R/i+/i-/C) loses signal between outdoor and indoor for >60 sec.

fixSteps.title: Polarity
fixSteps.instruction: i+ to i+, i- to i-.

whenToCallPro: Wire run fixes may need tech.
